resources.string: Play away from home
Step %1$d of 3

Prepare at home

Pair this device with your PC on your home network and confirm a normal stream works. Keep the PC awake and the host running.

Remote Wake-on-LAN needs a compatible router or an always-on device at home; the phone cannot wake an unreachable PC by itself.

Connect your devices

A private VPN such as Tailscale can connect your phone and PC without exposing the host’s web UI to the Internet. Install it on both devices, sign into your own account and enable their connection. Existing VPN setups can also be used.

The link opens the official download guide. This app does not install software, create accounts, change router settings or enable port forwarding.

Verify from another network

Add the PC’s VPN address using Add address, with its streaming HTTP port if customized. This updates the saved PC when its identity matches. Return here afterward.

Disconnect from your home Wi-Fi and use mobile data or another network. Test checks the paired PC’s identity and five small HTTPS requests; it does not start a stream or download a speed-test file. A test at home alone does not prove Internet reachability.
Open Tailscale setup
Add VPN or remote address
Test this PC
Previous
Next
Pair this PC locally first. Its saved certificate and HTTPS port are required to verify that the remote address reaches your PC.
The PC responded, but this device is no longer paired. Pair again at home before testing remote play.
The paired PC responded, but this device cannot view streams. Enable viewing or launching applications for this device in your host’s settings or web UI.
Checking your paired PC…
Test cancelled. No host or network settings were changed.

The paired PC could not be verified. Check that it is awake, the host and VPN are running, and the saved address and streaming ports are correct. If pairing changed, pair again at home. This test cannot distinguish a sleeping PC from a blocked route.
The paired PC responded on this network. Next, try a normal stream at a modest bitrate; HTTPS reachability does not verify video/audio UDP ports or sustained streaming performance.
Tailscale reports a direct path for this connection. Direct paths usually provide the best throughput and latency.
Tailscale reports a DERP relay. It provides connectivity, but streaming speed may be limited. Check Tailscale’s connectivity guidance or configure a suitable peer relay.
Tailscale reports a peer relay. Performance depends on that relay and both network paths; compare a real stream.
Direct or relayed path: unavailable. This host, VPN or connection does not expose a current route classification. Check your VPN’s status; low ping alone does not prove a direct path.
HTTPS request average: %1$.1f ms\nFailed requests: %2$.0f %%\nThese are application-request measurements, not video packet loss or input latency.
